channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] 36 years later: Hungary opens Communist-era secret service files
item.description: Decades after the end of Soviet rule, Hungary is releasing all its secret service files. The disclosure is sparking fresh debate about informants, guilt and responsibility.

item.title: [DW] Kosovo: Outrage as authorities accused of not helping femicide victim
item.description: Despite reporting her husband to the police and pleading for protection, Arlinda Zekaj was brutally murdered. Now, thousands in Kosovo are protesting what they say is a dramatic failure of state institutions.

item.title: [DW] Cyprus: From ties with Russia to a strategic alignment with the US
item.description: The Republic of Cyprus long balanced ties between Russia and the West. Now, it is phasing out Russian weapons, expanding defense cooperation with the United States and redefining its place in the Eastern Mediterranean.

item.title: [DW] Multiple flights to European airports targeted by bomb threats
item.description: The bomb threats involved two passenger planes bound for Warsaw, a Ryanair flight from London to Spain, two flights to Rome and a flight traveling from Israel to the Bulgarian capital, Sofia. No explosives were found.

item.title: [DW] Could the AI boom make borrowing more expensive in Europe?
item.description: France, Germany and Italy face a volatile bond market as war inflation bites. With US tech giants now issuing billions in AI bonds, they are competing with cash-strapped European governments.

item.title: [DW] Arrests and investigations as Serbia begins postelection cleanup
item.description: The landslide victory of the Student List in Serbia's general election seems to have removed a blockage in the justice system: Cases that were long stalled are now suddenly moving forward.

item.title: [DW] Bomb threats disrupt several flights across Europe
item.description: At least a dozen flights were either diverted or landed with a military escort after bomb or security threats. The first reported case involved a flight from Dublin to Rome landing outside Paris and more soon followed.

item.title: [EU Observer] Internal energy papers show “half-hearted” EU commission efforts to save methane rules
item.description: As ambassadors meet again to decide how long to delay the EU’s methane rules, internal documents show how the commission did too little to save them.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: Drug trafficking is ramping up in Europe, why and what are the consequences ?
item.description: The trial of 5 men suspected of brutal killings associated with France’s major drug cartel should come to an end in Aix-en Provence this Friday (6th of November).

item.title: [EU Observer] Europe’s democratic renewal is coming from the margins — and Brussels still isn’t listening
item.description: None of Serbia, Albania or Bosnia and Herzegovina are full EU members. Brussels generally approaches them as recipients of European democratic standards, not as teachers. But what if Europe's democratic renewal comes not from its political centres, but from its edges?

item.title: [Politico Europe] Security Sunday: Die neue Front der Bundeswehr in Litauen – mit Robertas Kaunas
item.description: Eingeklemmt zwischen Kaliningrad und Belarus liegt die verwundbarste Stelle der NATO. Genau hier entsteht mit der Panzerbrigade 45 das wohl wichtigste Projekt der deutschen Zeitenwende. Bis 2027 sollen fast 5.000 deutsche Soldaten dauerhaft in Litauen stationiert werden. Doch die Bedrohung durch Russland ist längst nicht mehr nur theoretisch: Drohnen, Desinformation und brennende Infrastruktur zeigen, dass […]

item.title: [Euractiv] Serbia’s student victory leaves Kosovo Serbs facing uncertainty
item.description: Belgrade funds healthcare, education, pensions and social assistance for Kosovo's Serbs

item.title: [Financial Times] Crypto industry braces for reckoning over Trump ties
item.description: Democrats have vowed to start investigation into president’s family after sweeping victory in midterms

item.title: [Financial Times] ‘Radical left’ get the headlines but centrists dominate new US Congress
item.description: Most of the Democrats who swept to power in the midterms blue wave are moderates

item.title: [Financial Times] Is Europe getting serious about ending tech dependence?
item.description: Brussels is moving in the right direction but could push national governments further

item.title: [Financial Times] America is craving a return to community
item.description: The midterms are only the latest sign of hope

item.title: [Financial Times] Apple saves $2.7bn in taxes by booking profits in Singapore
item.description: City-state overtakes Ireland as iPhone maker’s biggest tax shelter according to new disclosures

item.title: [Financial Times] Russia races to build rival to Elon Musk’s Starlink
item.description: Moscow’s flagship space project would enable more deadly drone strikes deep inside Ukraine

item.title: [Financial Times] Trump asks UFC boss Dana White to be new press secretary
item.description: US president signals combative approach in wake of midterms drubbing of his party

item.title: [DW] Armenia's selective prosecution: A threat to EU relations?
item.description: While Brussels has refrained from harsh criticism, Armenian civil society has warned of selective justice against opposition figures. Could the EU's pragmatic stance risk repeating past mistakes?

item.title: [DW] Journalism and AI: Who owns the news?
item.description: Publishers say AI chatbots are using their reporting to answer readers' questions while sending back less traffic and less money. Should the companies that build these tools pay for the journalism they rely on?

item.title: [DW] Son of Iran's shah receives 'Freedom Prize' in Frankfurt
item.description: 18,000 people gathered in Frankfurt to show support for Reza Pahlavi, the son of the Iranian monarch ousted in 1979. Factions in the opposition have accused him of not distancing himself from his father's rule.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine: Russia hits Kyiv with airstrikes ahead of trilateral talks
item.description: The strikes hit a major bridge and energy facilities in the Kyiv region. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Moscow of trying to "push" Ukraine "into a blackout" ahead of talks in Abu Dhabi.

item.title: [DW] Amid protests, France's rising debt costs threaten stability
item.description: France plans to spend an extra €4 billion on education amid nationwide protests. But with public debt mounting and interest costs climbing, how much fiscal room does the government have?

item.title: [Financial Times] Israel’s president gives Gadi Eisenkot first chance at forming a government
item.description: Isaac Herzog’s decision means opposition politician has 28 days to attempt to put together a ruling coalition

item.title: [Euractiv] Gunman ‘fascinated by far-right’ kills six in Krakow, Poland
item.description: Tusk called the shooting an act of "terrorism"

item.title: [Financial Times] What will a Democratic Congress mean for Ukraine?
item.description: With Donald Trump retaining control of foreign policy, lawmakers will use legislative tools to try to support Kyiv

item.title: [Euractiv] Commission opens roaming talks with Western Balkans countries
item.description: Move welcomed by travellers also carries political significance

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘A photograph allows us to really stare’: new Brussels exhibition documents modern human slavery, ahead of EU Parliament debate
item.description: A Brussels photography exhibition on modern slavery opened this week, exposing the cruelty of contemporary human-trafficking, often against women and girls, ahead of MEP discussions on the EU's new strategy.

item.title: [Euractiv] A tale of two bubbles
item.description: The AI bubble will devastate Europe when it bursts. Why is Brussels inflating it?

item.title: [Politico Europe] Ein Spaziergang mit Bodo Ramelow
item.description: Die Welt spielt verrückt, doch im Präsidium des Bundestages herrscht überraschende Einigkeit. Bundestagsvizepräsident Bodo Ramelow (Die Linke) gibt im Gespräch mit Gordon Repinski einen seltenen Einblick in die überparteiliche Zusammenarbeit, auch bei Nachtschichten. Dabei wird deutlich, mit welcher Strategie das Gremium den Provokationen der AfD begegnet. In seiner eigenen Partei brodelt es derweil gewaltig. Ramelow […]

item.title: [DW] Global pedestrian Karl Bushby returns home to UK after 28-year trek
item.description: Karl Bushby, a British man who traveled 50,000 km without transport over the past 28 years, has come home. Starting in Chile, he crossed the Americas, Russia and parts of Central Asia and Europe — almost all on foot.

item.title: [DW] How Iliana Yotova won the presidential election in Bulgaria
item.description: Iliana Yotova won the presidential election in Bulgaria, promising to be a "president of peace." But the campaign showed how divided Bulgarians are about the war in Ukraine and drone attacks in the Black Sea.

item.title: [DW] Czech arms makers set sights on space defense in bid to sustain Ukraine-driven arms boom
item.description: Czech arms makers have thrived on demand linked to the war in Ukraine. To sustain their growth, they need to look beyond ammunition and toward new technologies — and even space.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Merz’s conservatives poised to nominate Germany’s first woman president
item.description: Bavarian politician Ilse Aigner is "the perfect candidate," according to one center-left state premier.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Trump’s ‘big, beautiful’ European security plan isn’t convincing Europe
item.description: Capitals fear a U.S. effort to overhaul the continent's security arrangements could exclude allies and favor Russia.

item.title: [Euractiv] Dutch, Spanish candidates will vie to succeed ECB’s Lagarde
item.description: EU leaders are aiming to agree on Lagarde's successor by December, potentially as part of a wider ECB leadership shake-up

item.title: [Politico Europe] NATO faces €7B shortfall on military aid pledge to Ukraine
item.description: The shortfall sends a negative signal to Kyiv as it faces constant Russian attacks.

item.title: [Euractiv] Editors’ Choice: Less is now more
item.description: The Friday edition of our PM newsletter looks at the week that was in European politics and policy

item.title: [Politico Europe] Wave of bomb threats target Irish media outlets and more European flights
item.description: The latest spate of threats comes just days before a meeting of the European Political Community in Dublin.

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU capitals urge Brussels to ‘swiftly’ sign electricity deal with UK
item.description: The agreement could bring down U.K. electricity prices, but progress has been slow.

item.title: [Euractiv] Ireland suspects ‘co-ordinated’ campaign as Europe bomb hoaxes widen
item.description: Dozens of flights disrupted across Europe as authorities struggle to trace those behind the false alarms

item.title: [Euractiv] Europe rebuffs US push for new ‘security architecture’ in Russia deal
item.description: Kallas insists Putin has no veto over European security and warns against rewriting existing arrangements

item.title: [Politico Europe] Spain and the Netherlands battle over ECB presidency
item.description: Pablo Hernández de Cos and Klaas Knot are in the hunt for the top job after Christine Lagarde's exit.

item.title: [EU Observer] Italy still obstructing asylum returns from other EU states amid simmering dispute that threatens Schengen
item.description: Italy's foot-dragging on taking back asylum seekers from other EU states is contributing to a simmering dispute that risks shattering whatever trust has been restored among member states on the Schengen border-free travel zone.

item.title: [Politico Europe] ‘I don’t know if it reassured or worried them’: European envoys quiz Le Pen over lunch
item.description: The far-right candidate briefed ambassadors from France’s neighboring countries about her EU agenda.

item.title: [Euractiv] Poland urges faster EU social media ban for kids
item.description: Warsaw also wants simpler rules banning social media for under 15s

item.title: [Politico Europe] US officials head to Berlin for drug pricing talks
item.description: Talks come as Germany scrambles to avoid U.S. tariffs over the way it prices new drugs.

item.title: [EU Observer] Trump vows ‘beautiful’ Russia deal, as EU agonises over which envoy to send to Ukraine peace talks
item.description: Discussions on the EU envoy will take place at an informal summit in Dublin on 13 November, after Italian prime minister Giorgia Meloni bewailed the current "disarray" of various European diplomatic formats on the war.

item.title: [Euractiv] Mélenchon takes aim at the EU
item.description: The far-left leader is ready to ‘take on’ Brussels with a French ‘front of refusal’

item.title: [EU Observer] EU prosecutors launch possible €110m fraud probe into Spain’s railways, after second lethal crash
item.description: Spain is under investigation for its spending of €110m in EU development funds granted for planned renovation of the Madrid-Seville high-speed railway line, following a second deadly accident on the high-speed line in 2026.

item.title: [Euractiv] EU’s animal testing phase-out hinges on regulators, not labs, says Tsiodras [Partner Content]
item.description: Parliament’s rapporteur on chemicals assessment reform says the bottleneck is no longer the science but the rulebook – and warns of a new patchwork across agencies and borders

item.title: [EU Observer] Russians repel attack by Ukrainian ground-robots armed with RPGs, in futuristic assault (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,716)
item.description: Ukrainian commander Andriy Biletsky is gambling on mass robot assaults to spare his soldiers’ lives, as Russian troops rush to prove on camera that they can still swat the machines from the sky and fields around Lyman.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU states back one-year methane delay, but leave door open for more
item.description: Member states agreed a one-year delay to the EU’s methane rules, with a built-in option to delay again next year.

item.title: [EU Observer] From India to Africa, renewables race ahead but Europe is lagging, IEA report shows
item.description: The Iran war has pushed governments from India to sub-Saharan Africa to build more solar and wind, with some regions almost tripling new capacity. But in Europe, that rollout is stalling.

item.title: [Euractiv] No ‘revolutions’ – EU aims to hold line at COP31
item.description: Beyond electrification, Brussels aims to keep existing climate commitments alive in Antalya

item.title: [EU Observer] Hungary’s communist secret‑police files go online – and a Fidesz MP is named by mistake (Day 178 of the Tisza government)
item.description: Budapest finally opens its communist-era files and trims money for cultural and diaspora projects. Prime minister Péter Magyar navigates a minefield where each disclosure risks empowering Fidesz loyalists and unsettling Hungary’s neighbours alike.

item.title: [Euractiv] Kushner invokes Cold War diplomacy for European security deal
item.description: Ahead of Abu Dhabi talks, Washington proposes a new security architecture for Europe

item.title: [Euractiv] Spain to pull olive oil from market as glut looms
item.description: Madrid orders mills to withhold 12% of production, angering exporters

item.title: [Euractiv] New probe by EU prosecutors into Spain’s fatal high-speed line
item.description: A second deadly accident in a year has ramped up scrutiny over the management of Spain's railway system

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: The mental health toll of Europe’s migration policies
item.description: Racism, violence, institutional abandonment and unbearable living conditions.  These are all factors that damage the mental health of migrants and exiled people. That’s exactly what migrants in Ceuta are experiencing since July.

item.title: [EU Observer] After students voted out Vučić, can Serbia’s uprising against ‘evil’ change how the state really works?
item.description: The student movement's triumph over Aleksandar Vučić has built an unprecedented pro-democracy political momentum in Serbia. Their win follows two years of government crackdowns on protests kick-started by the Novi Sad railway station disaster two years ago.

item.title: [EU Observer] Trump’s mid-term election disaster is not good news for Nato or Ukraine
item.description: European governments may draw the wrong lesson. Americans voted on Tuesday about inflation, the Iran war and Trump himself, not about European security. Europe should not behave as if they had.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Investigation] How the EU’s methane rules came undone, and ended up giving Trump exactly what he wanted
item.description: The Trump administration wanted the EU’s methane rules gone. Internal documents show how the commission tried, and failed, to hold the line.
